From: Theo Ramos <theo@orcahealth.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity planning for MAP - Orca Health pilot

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re excited to move forward but need to lock down capacity details in the MAP so we can coordinate procurement and our internal security review. High level:

- Pilot scope: 3 inference models (2 chat assistants, 1 reranker)
- Expected steady-state QPS during pilot: 40 requests/sec (avg prompt + response ~ 420 tokens)
- Peak bursts: up to ~120 requests/sec for 10–15 minute windows during targeted promos
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for chat generation

Two asks from our side to finalize the MAP this week:
1) Recommended Dedicated GPU pool sizing (modeling for H100s or equivalent) and how you recommend we tranche reservations (staged vs all-in).
2) Lead times for Dedicated/Private provisioning (we’ll be on a VPC-connected private deployment) — we need expected provisioning windows so procurement can align with our fiscal quarter.

Also looping in procurement (procurement@orcahealth.ai) on timeline questions. If you can share a short MAP spreadsheet with milestones (evaluation, SOC2 evidence gating, contract sign, capacity reservation, cutover), that will help our PMs.

Thanks,
Theo Ramos
VP Product
Orca Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Theo Ramos <theo@orcahealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Capacity planning for MAP - Orca Health pilot

Theo — thanks for the clear ask and good to hear you want to lock the MAP this week. I put together a first-pass mutual action plan and capacity sizing rationale below. I’ve attached a one-tab MAP workbook (Orca_MAP_v1.xlsx) and an evidence checklist for SOC2/infra items.

Key assumptions (from your notes + our pre-demo sizing):
- Average request = 420 tokens (prompt+response)
- Steady QPS = 40 req/s; Burst QPS = 120 req/s for ~15 minutes
- Model family: c7-style Llama2-70B equivalent performance; inference optimized with int8/quantization where feasible

Sizing recommendation (Dedicated H100 pool):
- Baseline reserve: 4 H100s for steady-state (continuous throughput with batching & KV caching enabled)
- Buffer for bursts & headroom: +2 H100s (reserve total = 6 H100s)
- Canary/training node: +1 smaller GPU (A10 equivalent) for pre-production tests / model warmup (optional)
- Notes: with our batching + KV cache we typically see 1.8–2.5x efficiency vs naive per-request execution depending on prompt entropy; 6 H100s gives ~1.5x headroom for the burst profile you described.

Suggested reservation phasing (mutual action plan):
1) Evaluation (2–3 weeks): small dedicated test lane (1 H100 + staging A10) to validate latency and correctness with your prompts.
2) Pilot tranche (4–6 weeks): increase to 3 H100s and run production-like traffic for soak testing.
3) Full pilot reserve (go-live): scale to 6 H100s for the pilot period and monitor.

Lead times and procurement windows (Private/VPC deployment):
- Standard lead time for a Dedicated H100 tranche: 4–8 weeks from signed order to fully provisioned (depends on region and cloud vendor inventory).
- If you need accelerated delivery we can prioritize within our next-month capacity planning but that typically requires a 15% expedited allocation fee and a firm commit window.
- On-prem/VPC appliances: 8–12 weeks including networking and KMS integration (longer if there’s air-gap requirements).

MAP milestones (high level):
- Week 0: Sign MAP & NDA (if needed) — attach MSA & Order Form to HubSpot
- Week 1: Evaluation lane provisioned (1 H100) + SOC2 evidence kickoff (we’ll share checklist)
- Week 2–4: Evaluation tests, perf tuning, and acceptance criteria defined (p95 latency, throughput, token costs)
- Week 5–8: Pilot tranche (3 H100) + canary ramp & SLO measurement
- Week 9: Expand to full pilot reserve (6 H100) + production cutover plan

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- p95 token gen latency < 300ms on test harness
- Throughput validated at 40 QPS sustained for 60 minutes with <5% error rate
- SOC2 evidence items collected for infra and runtime logging

Attachments in this thread: Orca_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP timeline + milestones), SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf (short checklist). I’ll also drop a HubSpot record link with the draft order and costs.

If procurement wants a formal order-of-magnitude cost range I can put that in a separate note — quick rule-of-thumb: a 6x H100 reserved tranche plus dedicated bandwidth + monitoring falls into the mid-six-figure ARR territory for the pilot tranche (I’ll share a ballpark on request).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm target go-live window (you mentioned Q3)? I tentatively modeled a July 15th cutover to match your PM note.
- If that goal is fixed we should aim to sign MAP and order by May 10 to hit provisioning lead times without expedited fees.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Karthik to scope the evaluation harness and Soojin to start onboarding checklist items.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
